common_name: World Cup Hosta (Deeply Cupped Bright Gold Giant Hosta)

planting.note: Divide and transplant dormant crowns in early spring or early fall, setting the crown at the depth it grew previously in moist, humus-rich soil.

directions: Give this giant hosta ample room and a partly to fully shaded site with rich, evenly moist soil, since the deeply cupped leaves scorch if the site gets strong afternoon sun. The bright gold, heavily corrugated foliage cups upward like a bowl and shows a powdery white leaf reverse, an effect most pronounced when clumps mature over several seasons. Pale purple flowers appear on tall scapes in early summer. Mulch to retain moisture and divide only when clumps become crowded, as this cultivar resents frequent disturbance.

common_name: Lakeside Paisley Print Hosta (Feathered Cream-Centered Compact Hosta)

planting.note: Divide and transplant dormant crowns in early spring, setting the crown at the depth it grew previously in moist, humus-rich soil.

directions: Plant this compact cultivar in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade, where the thick, puckered leaves develop their best feathery center pattern of cream and gold radiating over a deep green base. Light purple flowers rise on pale scapes to roughly two feet in midsummer. Because the clump stays small and dense, it works well near a path edge or in a container, and it needs dividing only infrequently. Water during dry spells, as the substantial leaves still wilt under drought stress despite their tough texture.

common_name: Island Breeze Hosta (Gold-Centered Green-Margined Small Hosta)

planting.note: Divide and transplant dormant crowns in early spring, setting the crown at the depth it grew previously in moist, humus-rich soil.

directions: Site this sport of 'Paradise Island' in part shade with humus-rich, evenly moist soil, since brighter light intensifies the bright gold leaf centers while deeper shade shifts them toward chartreuse. The thick, rounded leaves carry wide, dark green margins and red-speckled petioles, giving strong two-tone contrast through the growing season. Medium lavender tubular flowers appear on upright scapes in summer above the mounding clump. Mulch to conserve soil moisture and divide congested clumps in spring once every few years.

common_name: Miss America Hosta (Giant White-Centered Green-Margined Shadowland Hosta)

planting.note: Divide and transplant dormant crowns in early spring, setting the crown at the depth it grew previously in moist, humus-rich soil and allowing ample room for a mature clump.

directions: Give this large Shadowland-series hosta a partly to fully shaded site with rich, evenly moist soil, since the broad, heart-shaped leaves need consistent moisture to fill out their bright white centers against medium green margins. Thick, upright scapes carry near-white tubular flowers with faint lavender centers well above the foliage in early to midsummer, an unusually showy bloom for the genus. The clump grows vigorously once established and shows good resistance to common hosta pests. Mulch to protect the shallow root system and divide only when the planting becomes crowded, since it can take a couple of seasons to reach full size.

planting.note: Divide and transplant dormant crowns in early spring, setting the crown at the depth it grew previously in moist, humus-rich soil.

directions: Plant this Hans Hansen introduction, a cross involving 'Maekawa', 'Halcyon', and 'Salute', in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade to preserve its lasting blue leaf color through the season. The rippled, wavy-edged leaves emerge grayish blue in spring and shift toward blue-green as summer heat arrives, and the cascading habit suits a raised bed, ledge, or large container. Pale lavender flowers appear on arching scapes in late summer into early fall. The thick leaf substance gives good resistance to slug damage, and established clumps need dividing only every several years.

common_name: Skywriter Hosta (Ruffled Solid Blue Semi-Upright Hosta)

planting.note: Divide and transplant dormant crowns in early spring, setting the crown at the depth it grew previously in moist, humus-rich soil.

directions: Bred from strongly blue parents including 'Smoke Signals' and 'Neptune', this cultivar holds its solid blue, heavily corrugated foliage best in consistent shade with humus-rich, evenly moist soil, since the waxy bloom that produces the blue cast breaks down faster in hot sun. New leaves unfurl from purple stems in a semi-upright habit that displays the white leaf undersides as they emerge. Pale purple flowers appear on scapes in summer, complementing the blue foliage. Mulch to conserve moisture and divide mature clumps only occasionally, as the plant is a relatively slow spreader.
